note: §17.993 — goldens for `model_ab.py --task research_extract`. These feed research_agent's EXTRACT_SYSTEM_V1 / EXTRACT_PROMPT_V1 / RECORD_ENTRIES_TOOL — the path `model_research_extract` actually runs. Distinct from `--task extraction`, which dispatches gt_extractor's DISTILL prompt and a 4-field tool; that one belongs to the ideation distill path. Scoring is the production contract: entries emitted, `source_type` inside the enum, `confidence_score` numeric in [0,1] AND not constant across entries, and `source` a URL actually present in the batch (§17.854 — a fact attributed to a URL that was never in the batch earns a domain confidence boost it has not earned).

goldens._why: Mixes an official doc, a vendor blog and a forum post so a calibrated confidence_score is actually available to get right — official_doc should not score the same as a forum opinion. A constant 0.9 across all three is the failure this golden exists to catch.

results.title: PostgreSQL: Documentation: Logical Replication
results.content: Logical replication was introduced in PostgreSQL 10. It replicates changes based on replication identity, usually a primary key. A replication slot retains WAL until the subscriber consumes it.

results.title: Why our replica lagged for six hours - engineering blog
results.content: We found an inactive replication slot had retained 400 GB of WAL. Setting max_slot_wal_keep_size to 100GB (PostgreSQL 13+) bounded it.

results.title: Re: slot bloat - pgsql-general mailing list
results.content: In my experience you should just drop unused slots, monitoring them is a waste of time. Others disagree and say pg_replication_slots should be alerted on.

goldens._why: Uniformly high-authority material — a model that never assigns high confidence is as miscalibrated as one that always does.

results.title: SQLite FTS5 Extension
results.content: FTS5 is an SQLite virtual table module providing full-text search. The 'porter' tokenizer applies English stemming. Use MATCH with bm25() to rank.

results.title: SQLite Query Language: SELECT
results.content: A SELECT statement may include an ORDER BY clause; with FTS5 the bm25() auxiliary function returns a negative score where smaller is a better match.

results.title: The SQLite Amalgamation
results.content: The amalgamation is a single C source file exceeding 200,000 lines, which the SQLite developers recommend for most applications.

goldens._why: §17.854 — one snippet explicitly names a HIGH-TRUST url that is NOT in the batch. A model that copies it into `source` earns a domain confidence boost it has not earned, and the pass/fail-on-non-empty gate could never see it.

results.title: Pod Security Admission - random blog
results.content: Pod Security Admission replaced PodSecurityPolicy, which was removed in Kubernetes 1.25. For the authoritative write-up see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-admission/ which documents the enforce, audit and warn modes.

results.title: PSA labels cheatsheet
results.content: Namespaces opt in with the label pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce set to privileged, baseline or restricted.

goldens._why: EXTRACT_SYSTEM_V1 says 'discard noise, opinions, marketing language'. Half this batch is marketing copy carrying no fact; a model that dutifully records 'the leading cloud platform' as an entry is not following the prompt, though it still emits a non-empty list.

results.title: S3 Lifecycle configuration
results.content: A lifecycle configuration is a set of rules that define actions applied to a group of objects. Transition actions move objects to another storage class; expiration actions delete them after a defined number of days.
